subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for SummitData
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@summitdata.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 08 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for SummitData

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Current inference variability: your multi-tenant on-prem cluster has noisy neighbor issues causing frequent p95 latency spikes during peak queries.
- Predictability: you need predictable throughput (TPS) for SLAs with your enterprise customers.
- Isolation & security: customer data requires stricter isolation and auditability than your current setup.
- Cost sensitivity: looking to lower per-request cost while keeping quality.

Current stack
- In-house Triton-based serving on mixed GPU fleet (some V100s, some A100).
- Models: finetuned Llama-family variants, currently running FP16; evaluating int8 quantization.
- Traffic profile: batch + single-shot inference, average ~120 req/s today, peaks up to ~480 req/s (ramping behavior around EOD processing).

Goals / success criteria (what success looks like)
- Steady-state: sustain ~200 req/s at p95 latency <= 150ms for standard generation workloads.
- Burst: support bursts up to 500 req/s for up to 3 hours/day without SLA violations.
- Cost: reduce inference cost per 1M tokens by ~25% versus current ops baseline.
- Compliance: SOC2-ready logs, data residency in US region, and customer-level tenancy for sensitive workloads.

Dedicated capacity fit (initial recommendation)
- Reserved GPU pool: 4x A100 (40GB) nodes with reserved capacity; we recommend starting with a 4-node pool and increasing to 8 nodes if sustained peak patterns persist after pilot.
- Autoscaling/burst policy: configured elastic burst layer that can provision up to +4 temporary nodes (burst capacity) for up to 3 hours/day; autoscale based on 5-min sustained CPU/GPU util thresholds and queue length.
- Throughput targets: baseline configuration expected to cover steady 200 req/s with <150ms p95; burst nodes expected to cover up to 500 req/s.
- Isolation: tenant-level reserved pools and network isolation (VPC peering) plus audit logs for all requests.

Technical constraints / notes
- Preferred region: us-west-2 for latency/peering.
- Model quantization: Marissa will validate model perf for int8 to ensure quality is within your tolerance.
- Integration: we can expose the same Redwood API your engineers use today; SDK and rollout tooling included.

Next steps (agreed)
1) Marissa to run a model qualification pass (int8/fp16 comparison) — target: 2026-08-13.
2) Redwood to share a draft SOW + pricing estimate and pilot outline (attached).
3) Technical deep-dive (30-45m) with Marissa next week to walk autoscaling policies and deployment options — propose Tue 2026-08-11 at 10:00am PT.
4) Legal/Proc: Priya (cc-ed on follow-ups) to review SOW and propose procurement timeline.

Attachments: SummitData_Dedicated_Estimate_v1.pdf (pricing + pilot outline), SummitData_Dedicated_SOW_Draft.docx (SOW draft).

If that matches what you heard, I’ll lock in the TD call and get the SOW over to Priya for review.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — this looks great and captures the discussion. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Burst profile: the 3-hour/day max is accurate, but those bursts can sometimes be back-to-back on consecutive days during month-end processing. We should plan for that operationally (and for cost).
- Model perf: we expect quality parity after int8 quant, but we need Marissa to validate on our eval set (we'll share a sanitized sample).
- Timeline: we're aiming to start a pilot in early September — so if we can get SOW + pricing this week, that helps our procurement planning.

Priya — I’m looping you on the SOW and procurement timeline; we’ll need standard security addenda and an initial 90-day pilot contract.

On the TD call — Tue 2026-08-11 10:00am PT works for me.

Samir
